## Experience

### Community Program Manager
***UC OSPO Network*** [October 2024–present · Remote (UC system-wide)]{.cvdate}

- Community manager for the [UC Open Source Program Office Network](https://ucospo.net) and one of its two full-time staff
- Helped build six of the seven campus OSPOs, including planning and hosting each one's first in-person community meetup, finding local projects and maintainers, and setting up mailing lists
- Designed the onboarding pathway for new campuses: welcome packet, public guide to standing up an OSPO, and working-group integration
- Co-chair the group that oversees the network's seven working groups
- Project manager for [UC Open](https://ucospo.net/events/uc-open-2027/) 2025, 2026, and 2027, the network's annual in-person conference (~100 attendees, 50+ speakers): run the speaker pipeline from CFP to day-of, and wrote it up as a reusable playbook
- Co-organized three in-person Reboot the Earth hackathons, co-hosted with the United Nations
- Represent the network at conferences, including FOSDEM, PyCon, Open Source Summit North America, UN Open Source Week, FOSSY, and the Software Heritage symposium
- Built a monthly virtual meetup with a core of regulars at every session (20–30 people from UC, universities worldwide, industry, and civic tech); also run twice-weekly office hours and a weekly events digest
- Co-taught cross-campus workshops on Git/GitHub and contributing to open source with CURIOSS partners
- Created [repository templates](https://github.com/UC-OSPO-Network/templates) (README, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, LICENSE) for UC projects, later adopted as a CURIOSS pattern
- Migrated [ucospo.net](https://ucospo.net) to MyST/Jupyter Book; maintain its CI/CD (GitHub Actions, WCAG 2 AA audits, unit tests)
- Helped launch public community calls for the [Open Repository Browser (ORB)](https://github.com/UC-OSPO-Network/repofinder), an open source discovery toolkit
- Advise open source projects on growing their communities, including NSF POSE-funded projects
- Use agentic AI coding tools (Claude Code) daily for site, CI, and automation work; wrote ucospo.net's AI contribution guide

***[PyBay](https://pybay.org)*** [2024–present (volunteer) · San Francisco, CA]{.cvdate}

- Logistics for PyBay 2024–2026 (300–400 attendees): venue, catering, vendors, speakers, CFP review, and day-of operations
- Redesigned speaker intake to collect everything at submission, eliminating weeks of follow-up

### Docs Lead
***[Distribute Aid](https://distributeaid.org)*** [November 2023–present (volunteer) · Remote, globally distributed]{.cvdate}

- Set up API documentation and version-controlled docs from scratch for an open source humanitarian aid platform
- Mentored contributors across continents on technical writing, five via Open Source Explorers

### Developer Advocate
***Suborbital Software Systems*** [February 2022–July 2023]{.cvdate}

- Owned the developer docs: user journeys, tutorials, API docs, and accuracy and accessibility audits
- Livestreamed product features on Twitch and YouTube with guests from Microsoft and Wasm Labs
- Wrote deep-dive technical posts (including a five-part WebAssembly series) and Python and Go demos
- Found points of friction in the developer experience and worked with engineering to remove them
- Was the technical point of contact for developers building on the platform, in the community Discord and beyond
- Ran social media (Twitter, LinkedIn, YouTube) and wrote the monthly newsletter

### Mathematics Lecturer
***CSU East Bay*** [January 2019–December 2021 · Head TA 2015–2018]{.cvdate}

- Instructor of record for 15 sections across 7 courses; Course Coordinator for College Algebra
- As Head TA, supervised graduate teaching assistants and wrote program-wide exams
